title: More than Meets the Eye
description: Thorben Danke used ultraviolet-induced visible fluorescence photography to make this image of a wild bee's eye, which is surrounded by tiny hairs. Landmark scientific research published in 1969 found that insect eyes contain fluorescent particles that absorb UV wavelengths and reemit them as visible light. "A quiet reminder that nature still holds surprises when we look at it through a different spectrum," Danke wrote on Instagram.
translated_description: 托尔本·丹克使用紫外诱导可见荧光摄影技术，拍摄了这张野生蜜蜂眼睛的图像，其周围布满细小的绒毛。1969年发表的一项里程碑式科学研究发现，昆虫的眼睛含有荧光颗粒，这些颗粒能吸收紫外线波长，并以可见光的形式重新发射出来。"这静静提醒着我们，当我们通过不同的光谱观察自然时，它依然蕴藏着惊喜。"丹克在Instagram上写道。
